newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Jan 20.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Jan 20.

text.p: All major Mexican ports were reported open Monday, including two of the nation's three key crude ports that reopened over the weekend as winds relaxed along the Gulf of Mexico, the Communications and Transport Ministry said in its daily report at 1000 local/1600 GMT.

Dos Bocas in Tabasco state reopened at 0800 local/1400 GMT on Sunday, and port officials said the port was shipping loaded crude tankers that were unable to sail when the port was shut four days last week. In addition, the crude port Pajaritos in Veracruz was opened late Friday.
On Monday, Salina Cruz port in the Gulf of Tehuantepec was closed to smaller boats amid winds between 40 and 50 km per hour.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Gulf of Mexico, Caribbean and Pacific Coast.
A low pressure front mixed with humidity, drawing clouds and light rains along the coasts of Sinaloa, Nayarit and Baja California states.

A light cold front heading southwest sent cold air to the region, with winds from the northwest at 10 to 20 knots (19 to 38 kilometers/11 to 22 miles per hour) and waves five to eight feet high. Winds along other regions of the Pacific coast were measured at the 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 km/11 to 17 miles per hour).
Cold air combined with Pacific humidity brought winds and light isolated rains along the coasts of Tamaulipas, Veracruz, Tabasco and the Yucatan peninsula with winds at 10 to 15 knots.

Moderate convective activity was reported along the western Caribbean sea with slight clouds along the Central American coast with winds at 15 to 20 knots (28 to 38 km/17 to 22 miles per hour) and waves four to six feet high.
